source: USLE_Agriculture_KS08.xlsm (S. J. Thien, Kansas State University), sheet Practices (I102:L107, E111:I116), formulas Pfactor!H19:H22; NRCS Iowa FOTG Section I, USLE Erosion Prediction (Sept 2002), Tables IIIa-IIId
about: Management practices that reduce the erosivity of water moving across slopes will reduce soil erosion. Contouring, strip-cropping, terraces, and grassed waterways are all examples of erosion control practices used to establish the P factor. Contouring is tilling and planting across the slope rather than with it. Strip-cropping uses alternate bands of cover and row crops across the slope. Terraces are soil embankments that reshape slopes into a series of short slopes that slow water flow and reduce its erosivity. Terraces that open to grassed waterways further limit erosion.
equation: P = Ppractice * Pterrace. Ppractice = contour P x subfactor (strip-cropping, buffer strips), adjusted when slope length exceeds the NRCS limit.

stripMeadow.source: NRCS Iowa FOTG Section I, USLE Erosion Prediction (Sept 2002), Table IIIc
stripMeadow.label: Meadow in the rotation

bufferStrips.source: NRCS Iowa FOTG Section I, USLE Erosion Prediction (Sept 2002), Table IIIb
bufferStrips.label: Share of slope in grass buffers

channelGrades.source: NRCS Iowa FOTG Section I, USLE Erosion Prediction (Sept 2002), Table IIId

slopeLengthLimits.source: NRCS Iowa FOTG Section I, USLE Erosion Prediction (Sept 2002), Table IIIa
slopeLengthLimits.adjustment: Adjusted P = (allowable length x P + (slope length - allowable length) x 1) / slope length

notes: Strip-cropping P = contour P x NRCS Table IIIc subfactor for meadow in the rotation. With 50% meadow this equals the workbook's strip-crop values exactly.
Contour buffer strips P = contour P x NRCS Table IIIb subfactor for the share of the slope in grass.

When slope length exceeds the NRCS Table IIIa limit (contouring; total slope for strip-cropping and buffer strips), P is adjusted toward 1 for the length beyond the limit. Limits are 25% longer with at least 50% residue cover after planting. The workbook did not apply limits; they can be turned off on the page.

Terrace factors match NRCS Table IIId: closed outlets (also underground outlets and level terraces with open outlets) exactly, and open outlets by channel grade measured on the 300 ft (or one-third of the terrace) nearest the outlet. The workbook's open values equal the 0.4-0.7% grade column.
Terrace interval classes are labeled 225-300 ft and >300 ft as in NRCS Table IIId (the workbook said 225-330 ft). NRCS Iowa starts the second class at 100 ft; the workbook uses 110 ft.
With terraces, AH 537 uses the terrace interval as the slope length; enter it in step 3. The workbook applies the terrace factor whether or not a contour practice is selected.
